parts.t: Neighbourhood guide · City of Maple Ridge · Thornhill and 256 Street
Thornhill is used as a sub-area name on the MLS®, where it appears as Thornhill MR. The City of Maple Ridge publishes no boundary for it.
In the City’s description, Thornhill is mainly residential and heavily forested, has a number of farms and nurseries, and includes a large trail network on 256 Street.

In the Official Community Plan, Thornhill is a long-term Urban Reserve, and the City will not support urban development there until two things happen: its population passes 100,000, and the residential capacity of the existing urban area nears build-out.
The official anchors I use are Thornhill Park and Thornhill Hall at 26007 98 Avenue and Thornhill Trails at 10390 256 Street.

This page was prepared on October 17, 2026 by Jared Gibbons, a REALTOR® at Royal LePage Little Oak Realty, who has spent 11+ years in Lower Mainland real estate. Each fact traces back to an official source listed on the page. Boundaries and rules do change, so before relying on anything, check with the City of Maple Ridge or with School District 42.
General information only.
Not legal, planning or financial advice. Confirm zoning, plan designations, flood rules and school catchments before you buy or sell.

Plan

blocks.text: Official Community Plan Thornhill Urban Reserve

parts.t: Policy

Thornhill sits in the Official Community Plan as a long-term Urban Reserve. The plan does not support urban development in it until the City’s population is above 100,000 and the existing urban area is close to being fully built out in residential capacity
Before building

Before urban development can happen in the Thornhill Urban Reserve, the OCP requires approval of an amended Regional Context Statement by the Metro Vancouver Board, approval of an extension to the Fraser Sewerage Area by the Greater Vancouver Sewerage and Drainage District Board, and an area plan adopted by Council
Parcels
Until those conditions are met, the minimum parcel size for subdivision of land designated Urban Reserve is 2.0 hectares (about 4.9 acres)

Thornhill / Haney Place is route 748, a loop starting at Haney Place. It travels by River Road and 240 Street, then McClure Drive and Jackson Road, reaching 100 Avenue. Planning, zoning and flood

blocks.text: Planning and flood notes for Thornhill

parts.t: Plans, zoning and flood rules can be different for each lot.

The OCP designates Thornhill a long-term Urban Reserve. Supporting urban development there has to wait until the City has more than 100,000 people and its residential capacity in the existing urban area is nearly fully built out.

Before urban development can happen in the Thornhill Urban Reserve, the OCP requires approval of an amended Regional Context Statement by the Metro Vancouver Board, approval of an extension to the Fraser Sewerage Area by the Greater Vancouver Sewerage and Drainage District Board, and an area plan adopted by Council.

The area plan the OCP requires must include policies on residential development, land use patterns, minimum density and phasing, a fiscal impact assessment study, identification of environmentally sensitive areas, an agricultural impact assessment, an aquifer groundwater management study and a transportation plan that includes transit.
Urban Reserve land cannot be subdivided into parcels smaller than 2.0 hectares (about 4.9 acres) until those requirements are satisfied.
There is no Thornhill area plan that I could find. Albion, Silver Valley, Hammond and Town Centre are the areas the City updated plans for in 2025.

ALR: nothing official that I found says Agricultural Land Reserve land lies inside Thornhill. Since each parcel has its own ALR status, check the specific address on the Agricultural Land Commission map.
I found no flood designation written for Thornhill. The City publishes a Be Flood Ready guide for Fraser River flooding and monitors river levels.
The City notes that landslides and debris flows are a hazard in parts of Maple Ridge. Snowpack melting during warm weather is one thing it says can cause landslides.
I found no slope area named for Thornhill, so check the City’s maps for the exact address.
The City calls the Thornhill disc golf course uniquely hilly and forested.

Thornhill does not have a West Coast Express station of its own. Maple Ridge’s two West Coast Express stops are Maple Meadows Station and Port Haney Station, and the service makes five trips each day, Monday to Friday, departing Maple Ridge each morning and returning each evening.

FAQ
Where is Thornhill?
The MLS® sub-area name Thornhill appears on the MLS as Thornhill MR. No boundary for it is published by the City of Maple Ridge.
The City describes it as a heavily forested, mainly residential area with several farms and nurseries, and says the trail network is on 256 Street.
How do I get around from Thornhill?

Route 748 (Thornhill / Haney Place) goes in a circle from Haney Place. The route follows River Road, then 240 Street, McClure Drive and Jackson Road, up to 100 Avenue. It then goes through 256 Street, 98 Avenue and 264 Street to 268 Street, and heads home on 100 Avenue. Buses are about two hours apart, and some trips use Port Haney Station.
Timetable dates: 748, effective April 20, 2026. Check the current timetable.
Thornhill has no West Coast Express station. The nearest stops are Maple Meadows Station and Port Haney Station.
Which schools are in Thornhill?

I found no school inside Thornhill. SD42’s June 2021 review names Garibaldi Secondary (24789 Dewdney Trunk Road) and Whonnock Elementary (27471 112 Avenue) among the schools affected by future Thornhill development.
Catchments are set by address, so confirm a specific address with
School District 42 (SD42)
What parks, trails and library are there?
Thornhill Park and Thornhill Hall are at 26007 98 Avenue, and Thornhill Trails is at 10390 256 Street.
You will find the Maple Ridge Public Library at 130 – 22470 Dewdney Trunk Road. No other Fraser Valley Regional Library branch operates in Maple Ridge.
What plan covers Thornhill?

I found no Thornhill area plan. The Official Community Plan holds Thornhill as a long-term Urban Reserve, and urban development is not supported until the City’s population exceeds 100,000 and other conditions are met.
Is Thornhill in a floodplain or on a slope?
I found no flood designation written for Thornhill.
Per the City, parts of Maple Ridge are subject to landslides and debris flows, and warm weather acting on melting snowpacks can set off landslides.
Plans, zoning and flood rules can be different for each lot.
What are the homes and lots like?
The City describes Thornhill as heavily forested and mainly residential, with several farms and nurseries.
Subdivision of Urban Reserve land is limited to a minimum parcel size of 2.0 hectares, roughly 4.9 acres, as long as those conditions are unmet.
ALR status is set parcel by parcel, so check the exact address on the
Agricultural Land Commission map
. I don’t have lot-size data for this area.
